headline: Hormuz blockade sends KSE-100 down 3.56% as Brent tops $86 — the desk stays patient and leans toward cheap, covered-dividend banks, fertiliser and E&P over autos, cement and OMCs.
summary: The US naval blockade of Iranian shipping plus a new 20% Hormuz cargo toll pushed Brent to $86.57 (+3.9% on the day) and KSE-100 closed down 3.56% — a second straight sharp red session, with selling broad across banks, cement, autos, E&P and OMCs. The desk's own risk gauge sits at 59/100 'moderate' with conflict-stress pinned at its max, and macro has called the regime risk-off. Domestic anchors — a steady 11.5% policy rate, cooling 11.1% inflation, growing reserves, record remittances — are genuinely constructive and argue against panic, but none of that offsets a live, unresolved chokepoint crisis hitting the oil-import bill directly. The desk is leaning cautious: favouring names that screen cheap with covered dividends in banks, fertiliser and E&P, staying away from autos, cement, OMCs, refiners and power.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: Rate-carry quality and generally covered dividends stay intact, though banks led today's selling (UBL -4.7%, NBP -4.6%, AKBL -7.6%) — the desk wants to see the group stabilize before leaning in harder.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Domestic-demand defensive with low direct oil-import exposure per the macro read; still fell with the broad tape today (FFC -2.3%) but the underlying beneficiary case is unchanged.

sectors.name: E&P (upstream oil & gas)
sectors.why: Direct beneficiary of the Hormuz-driven oil spike on realized-price economics, though MARI/OGDC/PPL still traded red today (-2.4% to -4.2%) alongside the broad market — a fundamentals case, not sector immunity.

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: Imported-input costs and a fuel/inflation-squeezed consumer bite harder as oil spikes; GAL -8.0%, GHNI -8.7%, TRG -8.2% were among today's sharpest single-name moves.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Energy-intensive with imported coal/fuel cost exposure; DGKC -6.1%, MLCF -7.6%, FCCL -6.1% and CHCC -6.5% were among today's steepest laggards.

sectors.name: OMCs & refiners
sectors.why: Weekly-repriced fuel costs and circular-debt/margin risk in a volatile oil spike; the government's $6bn refinery-upgrade fast-track plan is a multi-year structural story, not a near-term offset, per macro's own read.

sectors.name: Power
sectors.why: Fuel-cost pass-through and circular-debt sensitivity amid the oil spike; POWER and KEL both fell hard again today (-4.6% and -5.2%).

watchlist.angle: Sits in a favoured sector (banks). The desk's own backtest shows UBL's consolidation-break setup (Donchian 20-day pullback) firing with a 76% historical win rate over 38 trades (+2.2% net/trade, 80% out-of-sample) — one of the strongest proven setups on the board. Fundamentals rate 'attractive': 8.4x P/E, 30% net margin, 6.7% dividend yield covered at a 56% payout. Results are due 2026-07-22, a near-term catalyst.
watchlist.risk: UBL was today's worst-hit large bank (-4.7%); a further Hormuz escalation, or a soft results print ahead of the 07-22 date, could keep pressuring the stock into earnings.

watchlist.angle: Sits in a favoured sector (fertiliser — low direct oil-import beta, domestic demand). Desk backtest shows FFC's 52-week-high breakout setup winning 78% of the time over 27 trades (+3.2% net/trade, 71% out-of-sample) — the strongest proven signal in the group. Predictability score 66.5, second-highest on the whole desk. Results due 2026-07-29.
watchlist.risk: The 82% payout ratio is stretched — a weak quarter, or a feedstock-gas cost shock tied to the oil spike, could squeeze the dividend story investors are paying for.

watchlist.angle: Sits in a favoured sector (banks). Fundamentals rate 'attractive' — a cheap 5.5x P/E and a 17.05% dividend yield covered at just a 22% payout, among the best-covered yields on the desk. The consolidation-break setup carries a 63% historical win rate over 27 trades. Predictability score 62.3. Results due 2026-08-28.
watchlist.risk: NBP's beta of 1.14 means it moves more than the market — in a risk-off tape like today's (-4.6%) that amplifies the downside faster than lower-beta peers.

watchlist.angle: Sits in a favoured sector (E&P) — a direct beneficiary of the Hormuz-driven oil spike on realized-price economics. The 52-week-high breakout setup carries a 63% historical win rate over 27 trades (60% out-of-sample). Fundamentals rate 'mixed but improving' — forward P/E 7.8x vs trailing 9.2x, 40% net margin. Results due 2026-09-23.
watchlist.risk: OGDC still fell -3.65% today with the broad market — proof a genuine geopolitical shock can swamp sector-level fundamentals; a fast de-escalation that cools oil would also remove the tailwind.

catalysts.event: Next weekly petroleum price review — high probability of a further petrol/diesel hike given the confirmed oil spike
SBP MPC — first FY27 policy decision; watch for a hawkish hold if the Hormuz shock keeps feeding into CPI
PBS July 2026 CPI release — first print to capture the fuel hikes and this week's oil shock

risks: The Strait of Hormuz blockade and cargo toll are live and unresolved — any further escalation (Iranian retaliation, a confirmed physical disruption to Pakistan-bound crude cargoes) pushes oil and the import bill higher and could extend the selloff.

Oil at these levels feeds through to fuel prices (next weekly review 2026-07-17) and CPI (2026-08-01 print), which could push the SBP toward a hawkish hold or worse at the 2026-07-27 MPC, undercutting the rate-relief case embedded in bank and fertiliser valuations.

Foreign-flow risk: today's global tape wasn't itself a panic reading (VIX +2.0%, S&P -0.8%) — Pakistan is currently bearing this shock disproportionately via the oil-import channel, but a broader global risk-off would compound it.
